title: PyTorch 2: Faster Machine Learning Through Dynamic Python Bytecode Transformation and Graph Compilation
problem: PyTorch programs cannot easily combine eager mode's Python flexibility with graph compilation's performance benefits. The challenge is extracting and optimizing operation sequences without requiring code changes or sacrificing dynamic execution capabilities.
motivation: Graph compilation provides substantial speedups for ML training and inference, but traditionally requires abandoning Python's flexibility; enabling both simultaneously would benefit the widely-used PyTorch ecosystem.
method: TorchDynamo watches Python code as it runs and automatically captures the mathematical operations PyTorch performs, converting them into a compact representation called graphs that optimizers can work with. These graphs are then compiled into fast machine code by TorchInductor: Triton code for GPUs or C++ for CPUs. The key trick is that all this happens automatically while Python code executes normally—no need to rewrite code or manually tell the system what to optimize.
key_novelty: Intercepting Python's execution at the bytecode level (the low-level instructions Python uses internally) enables automatic extraction and compilation of math operations without requiring code changes or sacrificing Python's dynamic capabilities.
contributions: TorchDynamo: a Python-level JIT compiler that extracts operation graphs through bytecode interception
TorchInductor: a backend compiler translating PyTorch graphs to Triton (GPU) and C++ (CPU) code
Robust graph capture with minimal overhead compared to prior graph extraction approaches
2.27× inference and 1.41× training speedup on 180+ real-world models, outperforming six competing compilers

metrics.speedup: 2.27× geometric mean inference, 1.41× geometric mean training on NVIDIA A100

primary_theme: Dynamic compilation for eager ML frameworks
